summary:
Earth Trend Detective is an interactive Earth-system analytics platform built for NASA Space Apps 2026 (“Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”). It helps users answer: what changed, where, by how much, and is the change statistically meaningful? Using NASA POWER open data (1981–present), the project analyzes multi-parameter time series for 201 target locations (81 provinces of Türkiye and selected countries/capitals worldwide) and presents results through interactive maps/globes, charts, comparisons, and downloadable evidence reports.

The system combines a processed MySQL data layer with statistical validation—linear trend (including per-decade magnitude), p-value, 95% confidence interval, and the Mann–Kendall trend test—to detect trends, anomalies, and seasonal/non-seasonal deviations. Users can explore parameters such as temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, radiation/energy, and cloud-related variables, compare locations, and review country/province summaries. By turning large NASA datasets into clear, comparable, and evidence-based insights, Earth Trend Detective supports climate and environmental awareness and decision-relevant understanding.
details:
What it does

Earth Trend Detective ingests and analyzes NASA Earth observation/model-derived time-series data to detect environmental and climate-related trends and anomalies for selected locations and time periods. Users can answer what changed, where it changed, the magnitude of change, and whether the change is statistically meaningful.

How it works

- Data ingestion & storage: NASA POWER daily parameter values are fetched and stored in a MySQL analytical database (e.g., nasa_power_raw, locations, analysis_results) for efficient querying and reuse; World Bank indicators are stored as complementary context (worldbank_indicator_raw).

- Analysis: The application computes trend magnitude (including trend per decade), p-value, 95% confidence interval, and the Mann–Kendall test. It also provides anomaly analysis (including seasonal and non-seasonal/monthly-climatology deviations) and comparative summaries across locations and country/province averages.

- Visualization & evidence: A Streamlit web interface provides an interactive control panel, side-by-side map/globe views (including year-based animated globe exploration), time-series and anomaly charts, comparison/location-scan tables, and downloadable/printable HTML presentation-report outputs.

Benefits and intended impact

- Makes large Earth-system datasets understandable, comparable, and evidence-based.

- Supports awareness and planning discussions related to heat, precipitation variability, drought signals, humidity/wind, and radiation/UV-energy context by highlighting statistically supported changes.

- Encourages transparent interpretation by pairing visuals with significance and uncertainty indicators.

Tools, languages, and technologies

- Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy (statistics), Plotly (interactive visualization), PyMySQL/MySQL (processed data layer), Requests (API access), HTML/CSS (report/presentation export).

- Multilingual interface support: Turkish, English, German, French, Italian.

Creativity and factors considered

- Integrates multi-parameter, multi-location trend detection with statistical significance in a single exploratory workflow.

- Combines processed-database performance, comparative views, and jury/user-oriented evidence outputs.

- Includes clear mode labeling (live/processed data, simulation/fallback, or pre-generated evidence outputs) and backup materials for reliable demonstration.
